selection.method: highest remaining verified actor-primary profiles after Batch 28

profiles.name: Guy Spaull
profiles.excerpt: Guy Spaull was a radio character actor whose surviving GRH work is concentrated in the Scotland Yard crime series Whitehall 1212.
profiles.bio_html:
Guy Spaull belongs to the New York radio repertory whose professional record survives most clearly through broadcasts and cast lists. His strongest GRH concentration is the documentary-style crime series Whitehall 1212.

The program dramatized cases associated with Scotland Yard's Black Museum and relied on restrained supporting actors rather than broad mystery stereotypes. Spaull's repeated casting placed him inside that continuing dramatic company.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 12 Whitehall 1212 performances credited to Spaull and one additional Matinee Theater appearance.

profiles.name: Harold Dryanforth
profiles.excerpt: Harold Dryanforth was a versatile West Coast radio supporting actor whose surviving work spans private-eye drama, anthology and suspense.
profiles.bio_html:
Harold Dryanforth worked in the professional West Coast radio repertory during the postwar years. Personal biography is limited, but his surviving credits show steady work across several major dramatic series.

Dryanforth appeared on The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, Columbia Workshop, Let George Do It, Lux Radio Theatre, Richard Diamond, Private Detective and The Whistler. That range reflects the flexibility expected of supporting radio actors.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves three Philip Marlowe performances credited to Dryanforth, two each on Columbia Workshop, Let George Do It and Lux Radio Theatre, plus additional detective and suspense work.

profiles.name: Ian Holm
profiles.excerpt: Ian Holm gave one of radio fantasy’s landmark performances as Frodo Baggins in the BBC’s 1981 adaptation of The Lord of the Rings.
profiles.bio_html:
Ian Holm was born in England in 1931 and became one of Britain’s most respected stage and screen actors, with major work for the Royal Shakespeare Company as well as film and television.

In the BBC’s 1981 radio adaptation of The Lord of the Rings, Holm played Frodo Baggins opposite Bill Nighy’s Sam. The performance became one of the defining audio interpretations of Tolkien’s central character.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 installments of The Lord of the Rings featuring Holm as Frodo, documenting a major radio role within his distinguished acting career.

profiles.name: Jack Thomas
profiles.excerpt: Jack Thomas gave Candy Matson one of its defining supporting characters as Rembrandt Watson, Candy’s witty best friend and confidant.
profiles.bio_html:
Jack Thomas is best documented in radio through Candy Matson, YUkon 2-8209, the San Francisco private-eye series starring Natalie Masters.

Thomas played Rembrandt Watson, Candy's close friend and confidant, a recurring character whose urbane humor and loyalty gave the series a distinctive social world around its detective plots.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 Candy Matson performances credited to Thomas, making Rembrandt Watson the clear center of his surviving GRH profile.

profiles.name: John Beal
profiles.excerpt: John Beal carried a six-decade stage and screen career through several eras of radio drama, from Box 13 to CBS Radio Mystery Theater.
profiles.bio_html:
John Beal was born James Alexander Bliedung in Joplin, Missouri in 1909 and moved from university studies into theatre before beginning a long film career in the 1930s.

Radio remained part of Beal's work across decades. He appeared in anthology, mystery and detective programs during the classic network era and later returned as a recurring performer on CBS Radio Mystery Theater.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Beal, two Box 13 appearances and additional work on Molle Mystery Theatre, NBC University Theater, The Railroad Hour and The Whistler.

profiles.name: Joseph Bell
profiles.excerpt: Joseph Bell was a New York radio repertory actor whose surviving work is especially strong in X Minus One.
profiles.bio_html:
Joseph Bell belongs to the New York radio repertory whose professional history is preserved more fully in broadcasts than in later biographical accounts.

Bell appeared repeatedly on X Minus One and also worked on Lux Radio Theatre, Gang Busters and Theater Five, moving between science fiction, crime and anthology drama.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves nine X Minus One performances credited to Bell, two Lux Radio Theatre appearances and additional work on Gang Busters and Theater Five.

profiles.name: Mary Lou Harrington
profiles.excerpt: Mary Lou Harrington was a West Coast radio actress whose surviving work crosses comedy, Hollywood anthology and mystery drama.
profiles.bio_html:
Mary Lou Harrington worked in the professional West Coast radio repertory during the postwar network years. Her surviving credits show recurring supporting work rather than one continuing signature role.

Harrington appeared on Fibber McGee and Molly, Lux Radio Theatre, Let George Do It and The Whistler, moving between domestic comedy, feature-film adaptation and mystery.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves six Fibber McGee and Molly performances credited to Harrington, five Lux Radio Theatre appearances and additional work on Let George Do It and The Whistler.

profiles.name: Morgan Fairchild
profiles.excerpt: Morgan Fairchild made her radio debut on CBS Radio Mystery Theater and became one of the revival series’ notable younger repertory performers.
profiles.bio_html:
Morgan Fairchild was born in Dallas in 1950 and built her early acting career in daytime television, including Search for Tomorrow, before becoming a familiar prime-time screen presence.

She made her radio acting debut on CBS Radio Mystery Theater in 1976 and returned repeatedly to the series. Her appearances placed a younger television actress inside a repertory that mixed golden-age radio veterans with newer performers.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 CBS Radio Mystery Theater performances credited to Fairchild, documenting a distinctive radio chapter early in her national career.

profiles.name: Rita Lynn
profiles.excerpt: Rita Lynn was a flexible New York radio actress whose surviving work spans espionage, private-eye drama, science fiction and literary anthology.
profiles.bio_html:
Rita Lynn belonged to the New York radio repertory that supplied changing supporting characters across crime, adventure and anthology programs.

Her credits include Counterspy, Crime and Peter Chambers, The Adventures of Philip Marlowe, A Man Called X, Dimension X and NBC University Theater. The range of genres is the clearest record of her professional versatility.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves two performances each on Counterspy, Crime and Peter Chambers and The Adventures of Philip Marlowe credited to Lynn, plus additional anthology and science-fiction work.

profiles.name: Sidney Newman
profiles.excerpt: Sidney Newman was a supporting member of the Lux Radio Theatre stock company, frequently handling small roles and doubles around featured Hollywood stars.
profiles.bio_html:
Sidney Newman is best documented through Lux Radio Theatre, where weekly feature-film adaptations relied on a dependable supporting company around the major guest stars.

Contemporary cast records identify Newman repeatedly in doubling and tripling assignments, the kind of utility work that allowed one actor to help populate several scenes in the same hour-long broadcast.

Golden Radio Hour currently preserves 13 Lux Radio Theatre performances credited to Newman, providing a concentrated record of his work inside the program’s regular supporting company.
